ideas.title: Cast your own lead plates in the beach: press a pattern, pour, dig out what you made
ideas.critique: A liquid metal heightfield filling a pressed cavity, with a freezing front and a real body lifted out, is physics the island has never had, and the player gets a tool that works for any shape. The risk is that it lands as one more glowing hot-material close-up like the glass posts; it only pays off if the casting really is the hole the player made and the player can then use it.

ideas.title: Rock it free: heave on the beat with the friends
ideas.critique: Resonant rocking as a timing skill comes out of the solved wall forces, and it is the first island mechanic you feel through rhythm. It is a narrow next step of the stuck project and could easily become a timing minigame whose oscillator is tuned to one hole.

ideas.title: Singing sand: the beach squeaks under wheels and feet
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Live synthesised sound driven by per-contact shear is a sense the island lacks and a real break from the silent fixed-camera physics studies. Reading the soil by ear is a thin goal, though, and the stick-slip pitch mapping can easily turn into a fitted look-up rather than a simulation.

ideas.title: A plank under the wheel
ideas.critique: This is squarely on the road: a carried plank that see-saws and sinks under a moving load is a part the player will use for the big goal. As a picture it is expected (a plank, a wheel climbs on), so its surprise rests entirely on the plank failing in believable, varied ways.

ideas.title: The tide comes for the yacht
ideas.critique: Coupling the tide to the soil's strength gives the beach a rhythm the player can plan around. But a rising sea plane plus per-band soil constants is mostly a timed lookup, and a time-lapse of a waterline creeping up is a familiar shot.

ideas.title: The canvas glows: rebuild the yacht as a real built thing
ideas.critique: The last post was already a backlit patched sail on this yacht, shown standing still, so this would be the same still again with better assets. Diffuse transmission is a fair rendering goal, but nothing new happens or can be played.

ideas.title: Lumi digs like a bird: beak scoops, flying sand, a hole you can see
ideas.critique: It gives Lumi's own body a real action and conserves sand, both welcome after so many films with nobody in them. It polishes R-digging that already works, so its play adds little, and a few hundred ballistic grains is modest as particles go.

ideas.title: Tug of war on the beach: friends vs the bogged cart
ideas.critique: Friends whose pull is capped by their own footing, leaving furrows, is creature play with real soil physics and the question of who stands where. It overlaps the push and rock ideas as yet another way out of the same hole, and a one-axis rope chain is easy to rig for one case.

ideas.title: Planté fizz on the bench: form a lead plate by charging it
same_form: A top over a ring of lodestone
ideas.critique: It is an important part of the road, but as pitched it is the island's most worn recipe: an electrochemical device on the bench, left alone and filmed close while its state changes. Bubbles from the real current are honest, yet viewers have seen this shape ten times in a row.

ideas.title: Footprints tell who passed
ideas.critique: Real-shaped, weight-pressed prints across the whole beach that the wind smooths make a world that remembers, which is a lovely idea for reading the island. Its play depends on creatures doing hidden things at night worth tracking, and a still of tracks will read as decoration.
